scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

F-01.statement: Field route completion for Aug-Sep 2026 was 88% against a 95% target, covering 9200 manual-read accounts.

F-02.statement: CRM dispute volume was 610 (Jun 2026), 590 (Jul 2026), 1180 (Aug 2026), 1260 (Sep 2026), i.e. roughly a doubling from July to August that persisted into September.

F-03.statement: CRM dispute ticket response times (2440 tickets) show median 1.6 days and p90 2.8 days against a 3.0-day SLA.

F-04.statement: Disputed bills by read type: 1240 ESTIMATED and 1785 ACTUAL (billing-db).

F-05.statement: Billing-db tariff change log shows zero recorded tariff changes.

F-06.statement: Service contract §4.2 permits the utility to request route priority changes, executed only after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

F-07.statement: route-log lagging_routes identifies 14 routes with distinct completion values; sample record shows route R-00 at 0.70 completion.

F-08.statement: billing-db accounts_estimated_last_cycle lists 320 distinct accounts (40 distinct routes) estimated in the most recent cycle.

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

CL-03.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

H-SPEED-AND-AUTOFIX.statement: The dispute surge is primarily a response-handling/speed problem and an automatable billing-correction task, so an AI agent can auto-answer tickets and auto-fix the billing cause.

H-RULE-CHANGE.statement: A change to billing import validation rules around August altered how reads/estimates are accepted, systematically producing wrong bills.

H-AMI-DELIVERY.statement: AMI/MDMS read delivery from the vendor (H-MDMS-BILL nightly export) degraded or changed since August, increasing estimate substitution and bill errors.

H-FIELD-READ.statement: Manual field meter-read collection or the daily upload handoff (H-FIELD-BILL) degraded since August, forcing more estimate substitution and incorrect bills.

H-TICKET-ARTIFACT.statement: The apparent doubling in dispute tickets is partly a CRM reporting/categorization artifact rather than a genuine increase in incorrect bills.

H-FIELD-STAFFING.statement: Insufficient field reading staffing/headcount since August is the direct cause of missed routes feeding wrong bills.

H-ACTUAL-READ-ERROR.statement: A majority of billing disputes stem from errors in processing ACTUAL (non-estimated) meter reads (e.g. misreads or tariff application), not from estimate substitution.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Route-log shows field manual-read route completion at 88% against a 95% target for Aug-Sep 2026, covering 9200 manual-read accounts, i.e. roughly 7 percentage points of routes were missed in that window. This is consistent with reduced manual read collection feeding more estimate substitution during the dispute-surge period, but says nothing about why completion fell short (e.g. staffing) or about response speed/CRM artifacts.

Authoritative CRM data confirms the stakeholder's framing that ticket volume roughly doubled starting August (590→1180) and remained elevated in September (1260), establishing the surge as a real volume phenomenon rather than a mere reporting artifact; it does not by itself indicate why bills are wrong.

CRM data shows dispute ticket response times (median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days) are within the 3.0-day SLA across 2440 tickets, i.e. response handling is not slow. This undercuts the 'response speed' component of CL-01's framing of the dispute surge as a speed problem; it says nothing about why bills are wrong.

Billing-db shows disputed bills split by read type: 1240 tied to ESTIMATED reads versus 1785 tied to ACTUAL reads, so a majority (about 59%) of disputed bills are associated with actual meter reads, not estimate substitution.

The tariff change log returned zero records, indicating no tariff rate changes occurred in the period, which rules out a tariff-rate change as the mechanism behind the ACTUAL-read billing errors flagged by E-04 and narrows that explanation toward misreads or other processing errors rather than tariff application.

E-06.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL (non-authoritative stakeholder claim) states no tariff change occurred this year, corroborating the authoritative billing-db tariff log (E-05) that already shows zero tariff changes in Aug-Sep; it adds no new mechanism for the ACTUAL-read billing errors.

E-07.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD (non-authoritative, interview) claims the field reading contractor has been short three readers since July, causing routes to run late and those customers' bills to be estimated instead of actual. This is an unverified stakeholder-proposed mechanism directly matching H-FIELD-STAFFING's causal claim, but comes from a stakeholder with a stated incentive (contract headcount increase) and no supporting authoritative headcount or route-cause data yet.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: This document is a procedural/authority clause, not causal evidence: it establishes that route priority change requests from the utility must be executed only after confirmation by the Field Operations Manager, corroborating the existing K-DISPATCH constraint. It says nothing about the mechanism behind the ACTUAL-read billing disputes.

E-09.content: route-log.lagging_routes → 14 record(s); fields ['completion', 'route'] | completion: 14 distinct values | route: 14 distinct values | sample: {"completion": 0.7, "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: route-log.lagging_routes returns 14 individual routes with distinct completion values (sample: route R-00 at 0.70 completion), giving per-route granularity behind the aggregate 88% completion figure (E-01); it has not yet been joined to billing-db's estimated-account data, so it does not by itself establish whether these lagging routes correspond to the ESTIMATED-read dispute minority.

E-10.content: billing-db.accounts_estimated_last_cycle → 320 record(s); fields ['account_id', 'route'] | account_id: 320 distinct values | route: 40 distinct values | sample: {"account_id": "AC-20000", "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: E-10 is a raw billing-db pull of 320 accounts estimated in the last billing cycle (account_id, route; 40 distinct routes), supplying the billing-side dataset planned for the W-WI-1 join against route-log lagging_routes (E-09) to test U-FIELD-READ-CONTRIBUTION-VALI. It establishes no correlation by itself; note E-09 carries only route+completion (no account_id), so any join must key on route rather than account_id as the work item currently describes.

U-ACTUAL-READ-ERROR-MECHANISM.question: What specific mechanism (misreads, a billing import validation rule change, or another processing defect) causes the majority of ACTUAL-read bill disputes?
U-ACTUAL-READ-ERROR-MECHANISM.decision_impact: Determines whether any future fix targets billing-config rules, MDMS read processing, or billing-db logic, and whether a write_bill_adjustment is ever justified.
U-ACTUAL-READ-ERROR-MECHANISM.resolution_path: Query billing-config rule-change log (H-RULE-CHANGE) and MDMS read events for disputed ACTUAL accounts once vendor export access is restored.
U-ACTUAL-READ-ERROR-MECHANISM.safe_placeholder: Continue read-only diagnosis via billing-db and billing-config; do not build an auto-answer or auto-fix agent until the mechanism is confirmed by authoritative evidence.

U-FIELD-READ-CONTRIBUTION-VALI.question: Does the field route-completion shortfall (88% vs 95%, E-01) materially contribute to the ESTIMATED-read minority of disputes (1240), making H-FIELD-READ a worthwhile secondary line of investigation despite H-FIELD-STAFFING being rejected?
U-FIELD-READ-CONTRIBUTION-VALI.decision_impact: Determines whether field dispatch or staffing remedies (protected by K-DISPATCH) are ever warranted as a secondary fix.
U-FIELD-READ-CONTRIBUTION-VALI.resolution_path: Correlate route-log missed-route accounts with ESTIMATED-read disputed accounts in billing-db.
U-FIELD-READ-CONTRIBUTION-VALI.safe_placeholder: Treat field staffing/route completion as an unconfirmed secondary contributor; do not push any dispatch route change (K-DISPATCH) without correlation evidence.

U-SUCCESS-METRIC-PAIRING.question: Is dispute-volume reduction alone (G-1) a valid success signal, or must it be paired with the ACTUAL-read error share to confirm fewer genuine billing errors rather than suppressed ticket reporting?
U-SUCCESS-METRIC-PAIRING.decision_impact: Affects how success thresholds are set and whether a volume drop alone would be wrongly treated as problem resolution.
U-SUCCESS-METRIC-PAIRING.resolution_path: Track dispute_volume_trend together with actual_read_dispute_share before declaring success.
U-SUCCESS-METRIC-PAIRING.safe_placeholder: Report both metrics jointly in any status update; do not close the problem on volume alone.

A-ONSET-TIMING.statement: The ACTUAL-read billing errors driving the majority of disputes began or worsened around August 2026, coinciding with the ticket surge, though no evidence directly dates the error onset.

A-CRM-BILLINGDB-LINKAGE.statement: CRM dispute tickets (E-02) and billing-db's disputed-bills-by-read-type counts (E-04) refer to the same population of disputes, allowing the read-type split to explain the volume surge.
